instrument: tidycrm test: ten wheel ticks past each zoom bound through useWheelZoom's arithmetic (zoomAt + clampPose) leave the pose unchanged; red today, green once it passes rig bounds' zoom as zoomAt's fifth argument
title: tidycrm's wheel zoom slides the scene at a zoom bound, as the kit's did
body:
## Summary
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/space/useWheelZoom.ts:86 calls `zoomAt` and then `rig.set`, which clamps the zoom but keeps the pan solved for the unclamped zoom, so every wheel tick past a bound slides the scene while the zoom stands still.

## Description
The kit fixed this in ea815f2: `zoomAt` (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/camera.ts) now takes the bounds' zoom range as a fifth argument and clamps before it solves the pan, and the rig's own `zoomBy` passes it. tidycrm's space view has its own wheel listener (useWheelZoom.ts:86-92) that converts the anchor into its orthographic units and calls `rig.set(zoomAt(rig.get(), factor, anchor, frame))` with four arguments; `rig.set` then clamps the zoom in `apply` (useCameraRig.ts) and keeps the pan. canvas-graph/viewport-transform: "Apply the new scale (clamped to the min/max range), then recompute the pan" and "Clamp the scale in the authority, not at call sites". Fixed looks like: pass the rig's `bounds.zoom` (the same tuple tidycrm hands useCameraRig) as zoomAt's fifth argument.

## Flow
- the reader wheels in on the space view until the zoom reaches its maximum
- each further tick: zoomAt solves the pan for zoom*factor, rig.set clamps the zoom back, the pan keeps the shift
- observed (measured on the kit's identical arithmetic): ten ticks at the minimum moved the pan 600 scene units with the zoom unchanged
- fix: one argument at useWheelZoom.ts:86, plus the tidycrm test above

## Expected impact
A tidycrm reader who wheels past the zoom limit no longer watches the scene drift toward the pointer. Nothing else changes inside the bounds; risk is the orthographic anchor conversion, which the argument does not touch.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the scene stays put when the zoom cannot change
Before: kit arithmetic, same call shape: 10 ticks at min zoom 0.5 -> pan +600/+400 scene units, zoom 0.5
After: with the bounds passed (kit test camera.test.ts): pose unchanged after 10 ticks
Method: probe - the arithmetic was measured on the kit; tidycrm's own hook is another context's file and was not run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/space/useWheelZoom.ts:85-92 rig.set(zoomAt(rig.get(), factor, {...}, { w: box.width, h: box.height }))  // four arguments
examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/camera.ts zoomAt(pose, factor, anchor, frame, zoom?) // clamps z2 before the pan (ea815f2)
probe (scratch): 10 wheel-out ticks at zoom 0.5 -> pan {x:600, y:400}, zoom 0.5

instrument: desktop test (lib/bridge or stores/run) feeding the three bridge replies (unknown tool, unknown request, handler throw) and asserting the reason reaches the result row and the ledger; plus the CallReply doc comment
title: Let the desktop carry the bridge's unknown_ref and validator_failed reasons
body:
## Summary
inject.js now answers an unknown tool with reason unknown_ref and an unknown request or a schema-failing input with validator_failed (f3b82fd, c73569c), but the desktop records a page call's failure from `error` alone and still documents `timeout` as the only reason a page mints.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/lib/bridge.ts:56-57 says of `CallReply.reason`: "the only one it mints itself is `timeout`" - now false. apps/desktop/src/lib/execute.ts settleHostCall reads `answer.reason` only to detect a timeout and builds the result's error from `answer.error`, so the ledger row for a call to a tool the page no longer has reads as an uncoded failure, where the hands path (lib/hands.ts:198) already carries `reason` through. apps/desktop/e2e/support/page.ts:98 mimics "No tool named" without the reason. mcp-tools/tool-schema-design, "Two error channels": the channel binds the consumer too - a host that persists results without propagating the code rebuilds the ambiguity one layer up. Fixed looks like: prefix the error with the reason when one is present (`unknown_ref: No tool named x`, the form run.ts already uses), update the comment and the e2e mimic. apps/desktop is another agent's area this wave, so this was not built.

## Flow
- the page drops a tool between list and call (or the input fails its schema)
- inject.js answers { ok:false, reason:'unknown_ref' | 'validator_failed', error }
- settleHostCall keeps only error; the result row and ledger carry no reason
- fix: settleHostCall uses reason when present; bridge.ts comment; e2e page.ts mimic

## Expected impact
The ledger can group page-call refusals by reason as it does every other refusal; the model reads 'unknown_ref:' and re-lists instead of retrying. Risk: a test pinning the old error text.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a page refusal keeps its machine-readable reason end to end
Before: 0 of 2 coded page refusals reach the desktop result with their reason (read from execute.ts)
After: 2 of 2, by the named desktop test
Method: simulation - walked execute.ts settleHostCall with the three replies; the desktop is out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/lib/bridge.ts:56-62 '`reason` is present when the page minted one; the only one it mints itself is `timeout`.'
apps/desktop/src/lib/execute.ts:70 readTimeout reads answer.reason only for 'timeout'; settleHostCall error = answer.error
apps/desktop/e2e/support/page.ts:98 { ok: false, output: "", error: `No tool named ${name}` }
packages/athena-bridge/inject.js reason: UNKNOWN_REF / VALIDATOR_FAILED (f3b82fd, c73569c)

instrument: a JSON corpus (schema + inputs + verdicts) under packages/athena-bridge/test/ read by inject.test.js and by a new tests/test_bridge_input_parity.py that runs check_schema over it
title: Pin the page's input check to check_schema from the Python side too
body:
## Summary
inject.js's input check (c73569c) is a third implementation of the gate's JSON Schema subset; its fifteen pinned verdicts were taken from check_schema once, so a change on the Python side cannot fail any test.

## Description
src/athena/core/validators.py check_schema is the authority; packages/athena-bridge/inject.js checkInput mirrors it and must never be stricter (an input the gate accepts must reach the tool); examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/door.ts validateArgs is the page-side third. The JS test (inject.test.js VERDICTS) embeds the verdicts as literals. If check_schema gains a keyword or loosens one (the subset is 'exactly what the manifests declare' and may grow), the page would refuse what the gate now accepts and no test would say so. design-tokens/cross-language-token-parity strategy 3 and mcp-tools/tool-schema-design ("the published schema and the enforced schema must be the same artifact"): a gated mirror must parse the artefact both sides consume. Fixed looks like: move SCHEMA and VERDICTS into a JSON fixture; the JS test reads it; a Python test reads it and asserts check_schema gives the same verdicts. tests/ is outside this round's write set.

## Flow
- someone adds 'pattern' or loosens 'additionalProperties' in check_schema
- the gate accepts an input the page refuses: validator_failed at the page after a card was approved
- no test fails on either side
- fix: shared fixture, read by both languages

## Expected impact
A drift between the gate and the page becomes a red test in whichever language moved. No runtime change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the two validators cannot drift silently
Before: a seeded change to check_schema (e.g. maxLength ignored) fails 0 tests on either side (by construction: nothing reads the JS verdicts from Python)
After: the Python test reading the shared corpus fails on that seed
Method: simulation - the Python test is outside this round's paths; the corpus verdicts were probed with check_schema this session
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/athena-bridge/test/inject.test.js SCHEMA / VERDICTS (15 literals, verdicts from a check_schema probe this session)
src/athena/core/validators.py:50 check_schema
packages/athena-bridge/inject.js checkInput (c73569c)
